newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZOG says may speed Kupe production plans.
newsitem.headline: NZOG says may speed Kupe production plans.

text.p: New Zealand Oil and Gas said on Monday that it may bring forward its Kupe well production plans by two to three years which would bring forward substantial production cashflows.

Chairman Tony Radford told shareholders at the annual meeting that NZOG had re-assessed the potential for development of the Kupe offshore oil mining licence in Taranaki waters off the west coast of the North Island and under one new scenario production could be under way in three to four years.
The new scenario envisages a development initially based on oil production with most of the gas production re-injected into the reservoir until matched with demand.
This situation is to be decided on after the recent 3D seismic survey results are fully evaluation in the new year.
A gas contract is still seen as a necessary factor in proceeding in development and negotiations are again in progress on that front.
The results of the 3D seismic indicate that the Toru structure in the northern part of the licence had greater potential and may be comparable in reserves in the Central Field.

Commenting on the recent bonus options issue, Radford said the move may have been seen as unusual in the NZ market but share options are a common feature of listed mining and oil companies in Australia with about 30 percent of such companies having options on issue.

Radford said the recent short term outlay of cash for the purchase of 3.2 million shares in NZOG by an associate company was well within the capability of the NZOG Group, particularly against a background of $6 million in production cash flows in the current half year.

He said that once the company was re-registered under the 1993 Companies Act, it will be in a position to consider direct buyback offers, including pro rata offers to all shareholders. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
